page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the arm64 architecture. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The CPU configuration includes a 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and an 80 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong memory subsystem performance, with the PassMark memory score reaching the top 10% tier. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth is measured at 259.29 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reaches 113.31 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% tier. Computational benchmarks show average performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1819.28 and a multi-core score of 29084.31. Single-threaded gzip compression and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression both demonstrate strong performance in the top 25% tier, while database operations score 25751.53 on PassMark.

The c4a-standard-16 offers a cost-efficient profile for ARM-native workloads by utilizing dedicated physical cores without hyperthreading, which eliminates resource contention. This architecture is well suited for multi-threaded decompression tasks, database operations, static web serving, and moderate-scale Redis deployments. It is also capable of handling lightweight LLM inference, processing 1262.29 tokens per second for a 135M parameter model and 39.02 tokens per second for a 7B parameter model.
